SalesScenario.description: Represents a sales scenario in a business context.

description.description: A brief description of the sales scenario.
examples: In this scenario, the company experiences high demand for its products due to market trends and customer preferences.
In this scenario, the company faces low demand for its products due to market saturation and changing customer preferences.
description.title: Description

name.description: The name of the sales scenario.
examples: High Demand Scenario
Low Demand Scenario
name.title: Name

SalesScenario.title: SalesScenario

Source.description:
Represents an external source backing a quantitative claim in
EnvironmentScan or BusinessCase. Required so that "obtained from
external sources" is verifiable rather than merely claimed.

note.description: What this source specifically supports (which figure or claim).
examples: Basis for the projected 10% annual growth rate figure.
note.title: Note

retrieved_at.description: The date the figure or claim was retrieved from the source (ISO date). Required next to every external quantitative claim (ADR-0005): market figures go stale and the source alone does not say how old they are.
retrieved_at.title: Retrieved At

title.description: Short label for the source (publication, report, or site name).
examples: Statista: SaaS Market Size 2026
IBISWorld Industry Report
title.title: Title

url.description: Link to the source, if available.
examples: https://www.statista.com/...
url.title: Url

Source.title: Source

description: Represents a business case in a business context.

breakeven_formula.description: The formula used to calculate the breakeven point for the business case.
examples: Breakeven Point = Fixed Costs / (Selling Price per Unit - Variable Cost per Unit)
Breakeven Point = Total Fixed Costs / (Unit Selling Price - Unit Variable Cost)
breakeven_formula.title: Breakeven Formula

capital_and_operating_costs.description: A brief description of the capital and operating costs associated with the business case.
examples: The capital costs include the purchase of new machinery and equipment, while the operating costs cover expenses such as labor, utilities, and raw materials.
The capital costs involve the construction of a new production facility, while the operating costs encompass maintenance, staffing, and supply chain management.
capital_and_operating_costs.title: Capital And Operating Costs

funding_requirements.description: A brief description of the funding requirements for the business case.
examples: The funding requirements include securing a loan of $500,000 to cover initial capital expenditures and working capital needs.
The funding requirements involve raising $1 million in equity investment to support the expansion of production capacity and market entry strategies.
funding_requirements.title: Funding Requirements

id.description: Unique identifier for the business case.
examples: business_case_001
id.title: Id

market_benchmarks.description: A brief description of the market benchmarks relevant to the business case.
examples: The market benchmarks indicate a growing demand for eco-friendly products, with a projected annual growth rate of 10% over the next five years.
The market benchmarks suggest a declining trend in consumer interest for traditional products, with a projected annual decrease of 5% in sales over the next three years.
market_benchmarks.title: Market Benchmarks

profit_potential_notes.description: Notes on the profit potential of the business case.
examples: The profit potential is significant, with projected net profits of $200,000 in the first year and a steady increase in profitability over the next five years.
The profit potential is moderate, with expected net profits of $50,000 in the first year and gradual growth as market share increases and operational efficiencies are realized.
profit_potential_notes.title: Profit Potential Notes

project_id.description: Identifier of the project this business case is associated with.
examples: project_001
project_id.title: Project Id

sales_scenarios.description: A list of sales scenarios relevant to the business case.

examples.description: In this scenario, the company experiences high demand for its products due to market trends and customer preferences.
examples.name: High Demand Scenario

examples.description: In this scenario, the company faces low demand for its products due to market saturation and changing customer preferences.
examples.name: Low Demand Scenario

sales_scenarios.title: Sales Scenarios

sources.description: External sources backing the market benchmarks. A generation with no sources is treated as a failed generation, not as a valid empty result.

examples.note: Basis for the projected 10% annual growth rate figure.
examples.title: Statista: SaaS Market Size 2026

sources.title: Sources
